## Introduction & background

Puzzle days synthesize theory into intuition. The behavior of digital logic gates changes dramatically when combined with analog RC timing networks. A simple inverter becomes a relaxation oscillator. A NOR gate paired with an RC network and a control signal becomes a gated oscillator—a circuit that only outputs a clock signal when commanded. Finally, understanding AC coupling is vital for diagnosing why perfect square waves sometimes look distorted on an oscilloscope screen.

## What you're building

1. A paper-based architectural analysis of three distinct timing and logic circuits.

## Activity

Paper only, commit answers before any sim. (1) CD40106 inverter, R output→input, C input→ground: what is it, what sets f? (2) Swap in a NOR gate, drive its second input from a slow logic signal: what does that input now do? (What have you built — and how does R set the timing of the gated oscillation?) (3) A scope on AC coupling shows a square wave's flat tops drooping: which [Day 8](https://hardware.ellietaghavi.com/llm/day-08.md) circuit is secretly responsible?
**Then:** build (2) with the CD40106/4001 and check yourself.
